title: Best Photo Editors and Retouchers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a photo editor or retoucher: what the service should include, how to brief edits, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Photo editors remove backgrounds, correct colors, retouch portraits, restore old photos and prepare images for stores or print. Good editing looks natural and consistent across a set. It goes wrong when the style is not agreed, colors drift away from reality, or heavy retouching misrepresents products or people. This guide shows you how to brief edits clearly.

faq.q: What kind of editing do I need?
faq.a: Common types are background removal, color correction, retouching, object removal, compositing and photo restoration. Name the exact edits, since prices differ a lot.
The highest-quality originals you have, ideally RAW or full-size JPG. Compressed images from messaging apps limit what an editor can do.

faq.q: How do I keep a set of photos consistent?
faq.a: Edit one or two photos first, approve the style, then ask for the rest to match. Send the approved photo as the reference.
For products, edits should not change color, size or shape in misleading ways. For people, respect their wishes. Some platforms and advertising rules also limit misleading edits.

faq.q: What file format will I get?
faq.a: Usually JPG or PNG, with a transparent background if requested. Ask for the sizes your website or store needs.
